clue.text: Murder perhaps associated with a war zone

parts.note: murder is one example of a crime, hence the 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A killing that is linked to a conflict somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crimea was the scene of the Crimean War (1853-56) and of more recent conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula on the Black Sea has been fought over repeatedly, most famously in the nineteenth-century war named after it.

clue.text: Given energy again ere death possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim forecast: before dying, perhaps something happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Reheated food has been warmed up a second time, its heat restored.

clue.text: Male admires fantastic females in the sea

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man admires wonderful women out in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Mermaids are mythical sea creatures, half woman and half fish.

clue.text: Ace travelling to Saturn? Well, not quite!

definitions.text: Ace travelling to Saturn? Well, not quite!

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: travelling suggests movement, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A top flier heading for the ringed planet, or almost.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken whole, the clue describes a space traveller: none has reached Saturn, hence 'not quite'.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller might be an ace pilot bound for distant planets.

clue.text: Like a clique in the north about to engage in fight

indicators.note: to engage in something is to go into it, so the reversed pair is set inside the fight word

parts.note: a clash is a fight

indicators.note: about signals turning round the short run made of the words in and north

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Something cliquey up north about to join a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' applies to the short pair before 'to engage in', not to the whole fight, which wraps round the reversed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A clannish group sticks tightly together and excludes outsiders, the way a clique does.

clue.text: A blunt secretary comes out with various stories

indicators.note: comes out suggests the letters emerge in a different order

explanation.surface: An outspoken secretary reveals a range of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's fourteenth-century collection of pilgrims' tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's work is a collection of different tales told by pilgrims.

clue.text: No. 10 set up employment system

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is raised, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: number ten written out
work is employment

explanation.surface: Downing Street establishing a jobs scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 10 suggests Downing Street; it is simply the number TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is an interconnected system, as of roads or computers.

clue.text: What one needs to get fired up

definitions.text: What one needs to get fired up

parts.words: What one needs to get fired up
parts.note: reads as what a person requires to feel enthusiastic, but means what sets an engine or fuel burning

explanation.definitionFit: Ignition is the act of setting fuel alight, as in a car engine starting.

clue.text: Ready when plastic is unacceptable?

definitions.meaning: ready is slang for money available to spend
plastic means credit cards, so this is what you pay with when cards are refused

explanation.definitionFit: Hard cash is physical money in notes and coins, ready money as opposed to card payment.

clue.text: A throne's designed in eighteenth-century style

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are worked into a new pattern or arrangement

parts.note: the word throne with its s included as a letter

explanation.surface: A royal seat made in the fashion of the 1700s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges A THRONES; the S of the possessive counts here.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was a late Georgian furniture designer whose name labels that period's elegant style.

clue.text: A certain character, right person to make reparation

parts.note: tone is the particular character or quality of something

explanation.surface: Someone of a certain disposition being the right one to make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, so one who does so pays reparation for a wrong.

clue.text: Native chief additional to narrative

parts.note: a saga is a long narrative
more means additional, extra

explanation.surface: A tribal leader appended to a story.
explanation.walkthrough: A sagamore is a chief among some Algonquian peoples of North America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Algonquian title names a leader of a Native American tribe, a subordinate chief.

clue.text: Twitching when confronted by policeman's language

indicators.note: being confronted by something means having it stand in front, so the policeman comes first

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: Someone twitches nervously when facing an officer's words.
explanation.walkthrough: Coptic is the liturgical language of the Egyptian Christian church.
explanation.definitionFit: Coptic descends from ancient Egyptian and survives as a church tongue.

clue.text: Ward's disadvantage

parts.note: read the clue's word as is: the letters of the first half of the answer, taken backwards, give Ward

explanation.surface: A hospital ward's shortcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as instructions (draw, backwards) produces 'Ward', with the 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a snag or downside, the same as a disadvantage.

clue.text: Councillor in old cord skirt?

parts.note: a line is a cord

explanation.surface: A council member wearing an antique corduroy skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here; it gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinoline is a stiffened petticoat or hooped frame worn under a full dress.

clue.text: Name of man provided backing for love songs

indicators.note: backing something means standing behind it, so the man's name follows the love letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
Des is a man's name, short for Desmond

explanation.surface: A man's name supported love songs.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, often meant to be sung, so these are songs or verses.

clue.text: Number upset over the song being broadcast

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A musical number spoiled by the song that is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is going out live over radio or television.

clue.text: English company with no money starts to interest conglomerate in good financial shape

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their first letters

explanation.surface: A penniless English firm attracts interest from a big group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something economic pays its way and is financially viable.

clue.text: Sign of life in a new hospital accommodating a thousand

indicators.note: accommodating means housing something within, so the thousand sits inside

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: Signs of life in a fresh hospital housing a thousand patients.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the ancient Egyptian looped cross symbolising life.

clue.text: A good girl I left out, one girl in distress

indicators.note: out means taken out, so those letters are removed from the girl word

parts.note: the letter I as written
I is the Roman numeral one
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A well-behaved girl leaves, and another girl is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I and L from GIRL leaves GR.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to cause someone pain or trouble.

clue.text: Fuel — one reeks terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fuel that has a terrible stench.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil is burnt as fuel in lamps, heaters and jet engines.

clue.text: Heather goes to prison somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: the heather goes to the prison word, attaching after it

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
ling is a kind of heather

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather is sent to jail somewhere north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirling is a city in central Scotland, famous for its castle.

clue.text: Cocaine hidden in shoe? It's malicious gossip

indicators.note: something hidden in a shoe is concealed inside it, so the drug letter sits within

parts.note: a sandal is a shoe
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Drugs concealed in footwear, a juicy story to spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is damaging talk about wrongdoing, much like slander.

clue.text: Big shed in Elizabethan garden

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the run of letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A large outbuilding in a Tudor-era garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across elizabetHAN GARden.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangar is a large building for housing aircraft, essentially a big shed.

clue.text: Desolate area with stolen goods gone over in part of factory

indicators.note: gone over suggests the pair of words is turned over, read backwards as a whole

parts.note: a moor is a bleak, desolate expanse
loot is stolen goods

explanation.surface: Thieves' haul crossing bleak land to a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolroom is the section of a factory where tools are made and kept.

clue.text: An aggressive Philip used this weapon against girl

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the girl sits beside the weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A belligerent man named Philip wielded a weapon against a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip II of Spain sent the Spanish Armada against England in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip II of Spain launched his great fleet of warships to invade England.

clue.text: Being terribly tired, Leo dawdled

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Leo, very weary, dragged his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loitering is lingering idly, the same as dawdling.

clue.text: Don't destroy so much, we say — it's rash

indicators.note: we say signals that the phrase is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: to destroy less is to wreck less

explanation.surface: A plea to cause less ruin, because the behaviour is foolhardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rash acts without heed for consequences, which is being heedless.

clue.text: Small hole I mentioned having obstruction

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the letter is heard as a word of the same sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Someone notes a small opening blocked by something.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced opening for a lace or cord.
